jobs.title: Patient Advocate / Care Manager (Private Health Advisor)
jobs.description:
The Short Version

You will carry six to eight families. Not sixty. Not two hundred.

Part-time and hourly, or full-time and salaried: W-2 either way, and yours to grow at your own pace.

We have removed insurance mandates and hospital bureaucracy from the work. What that buys you is the rarest thing in modern medicine: the time to do the job the way you already know it should be done.

If that is the job you have been looking for, here is the rest of it.

The Role

Avoa Health is a private health advisory firm serving families on Chicago’s North Shore through serious diagnoses, complex conditions, and the challenges of aging. The Private Health Advisor is the single, trusted point of contact for those families. Their advocate. Their Healthcare Chief of Staff. The person who sees the problem coming before they do.

This is not case management. Case management is a caseload. This is a small number of families, held closely, over time.

Our clients are accustomed to excellence in every other part of their lives, and they expect the same standard here. One size fits one: every family receives a response built for them alone.

What You Will Do

Run central command.
You are the connective tissue between the family and their specialists, making sure every provider is aligned and the client’s agency is protected. You manage the scheduling, the records, the follow-up. Hushpitality is our word for doing that invisibly: the family experiences the result of your work without ever carrying the noise of it.
Vet the specialists. You evaluate physicians and institutions and find the right fit, not the nearest one.

Show up in the room.
You accompany clients to the appointments that matter, with the agenda prepared in advance, and you deliver a post-visit summary that turns jargon into a clear path forward.

Dismantle the roadblocks.
Pre-authorizations, denials, billing disputes. You absorb that friction so the family never feels it.

Build the scaffolding.
For clients facing cognitive decline or a difficult transition, you put discreet systems in place that preserve dignity while keeping them safe.

Own the problem.
Every issue is yours. When the system fails, you listen, you own it, and you fix it. You never say it is not your department.

Who This is For

You have five or more years in healthcare, ideally in advocacy, case management, oncology navigation, palliative care, or geriatric care. LPN, RN, or MSW is preferred and not mandatory.
You are warm. You are conscientious to the point that other people find it remarkable. You assume things will work out and you make them work out.

You can move from a technical conversation with a neurosurgeon to a briefing with a family office director without changing gear.

Your language is precise and generous. You know the difference between “I’ll try” and “I will see to it,” and so does the family listening.

You are comfortable with modern tools: secure video, shared calendars, the ordinary technology of a well-run firm. We provide the technology and the administrative backing so your attention stays on the families.

The Deal

Part-time roles are hourly. Full-time roles are salaried.
Both are W-2, which makes you a formal member of the team, not a contractor.
It grows at your pace.
Start part-time and grow into full-time as you and your client book are ready, or stay part-time for as long as it fits your life. Both are real, long-term seats.
Real control over your schedule, in both directions
. If you cannot take Tuesday mornings, we will not book you Tuesday mornings. In return, we ask for dependable daytime availability, since most of the work, care coordination and physician visits, happens in business hours, plus a willingness to help with the occasional off-hours emergency, which the team shares and covers together. We ask every advisor to hold at least one full day a week for Avoa Health, because that predictability is what lets us balance the work and protect everyone’s schedule. What you will not have is a pager, a quota, or a productivity metric.
Hybrid, roughly seventy percent remote
and thirty percent in person, flexing with what clients need. Our clients are concentrated on the North Shore, so plan on in-person meetings and physician visits in that area.
Travel is covered
. You will drive to client appointments; mileage between them is reimbursed at the standard IRS rate, and a company card covers authorized work expenses.
You are supported, not on your own
. Malpractice and liability coverage, secure technology, and full administrative backing, so your attention stays on the families rather than the overhead.
Full transparency before you invest an hour.
Before any formal interview, we put every parameter of the role in writing for you: compensation, schedule, technology, and the health and screening requirements. You will know exactly what you are considering before you commit your time. We think that is the only respectful way to do this.

Why Avoa Health

A return to the art of care
. You went into this work to help people, and somewhere along the way volume took the helping out of it. There is no volume here.

Autonomy with infrastructure
. You manage your own client portfolio. You operate with the independence of a private practitioner and none of the isolation, supported by the firm's systems and reputation.

Going above and beyond is the standard, and it is funded
. When you see what a family needs, you will not have to ask permission or find the budget.

Depth
. A handful of families, known well, over years. That is the entire proposition.

As a Program Manager, you join an exclusive team of leaders responsible for the implementation of the Alzheimer’s Association Portfolio of Community Program Offerings. jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
Case Manager Position

The Chicago Public Schools (CPS) has set ambitious goals to ensure that every child—in every school and every neighborhood—has access to a world-class learning experience from birth, resulting in graduation from high school college- and career-ready. In alignment with the mission of the Office of Diverse Learner Supports and Services (ODLSS), our schools strive to provide high quality and specially designed instructional supports and services for all students with disabilities within their least restrictive environment. We work collaboratively with the goal of improving the academic achievement of all students with disabilities by ensuring they receive meaningful and relevant access to grade level core instruction within their school.

The Case Manager position is solely committed to fulfilling the responsibilities indicated below. This position differs from a person at the school being assigned the duty/role of Case Manager that allows for the receipt of a stipend. The Case Manager position does not include a stipend.

The Case Manager position will be held accountable for the following responsibilities:

Serving as the local school district representative at all required meetings under the IDEA and serving as the 504 Coordinator for all meetings under Section 504
Fulfilling all the Roles & Responsibilities delineated in the ODLSS Procedural Manual for the local school district representative
Ensuring all IDEA and Section 504 timelines are met
Ensuring that all parental notices and consents for Full and Individual Evaluations and placements are processed and provided in the native language where feasible and placed in the student temporary files
Sending parents/guardians copy of draft IEP materials and if applicable paraprofessional, ESY ,and Learning Environment Intervention forms, along with copies of all other conducted evaluations and any other collected data at least five school days prior to the meeting
Ensuring an interpreter is invited to all IEP and 504 conferences (including initial and reevaluation eligibility determination meetings, and annual reviews) for parents who are limited English proficient
Coordinating all referrals for a Full and Individual Evaluation (FIE) to ensure that all required components are addressed and that the process is completed within 60 school days after receiving signed parental consent, including but not limited to, referrals for Assistive Technology/Alternative-Augmentative Communication evaluations or functional behavioral assessments (FBAs)
Convening and chairing IEP and 504 conferences (including initial and reevaluation eligibility determination meetings, and annual reviews) and acting as the District Representative
Ensuring that IEP teams are utilizing qualitative and quantitative data when making service decisions in the development of an IEP
Finalizing each student’s IEP or 504 Plan in the SSM at the meeting and providing the student’s parents/guardians with a copy
Ensuring that all relevant student data is entered into SSM in a timely manner
Arranging special education and related services for a student within the school in accordance with the students IEP and contacting ODLSS to arrange assignment in another school if necessary to implement the IEP
Consulting with the ODLSS District Representative regarding students who require low-incidence services or regarding problems that develop in the implementation of procedures
In collaboration with the principal, overseeing and ensuring the implementation of all IEPs and 504 Plans for each student with disabilities in the school
Training and supporting school staff regarding the implementation of the IDEA and Section 504 requirements
Attending all ODLSS professional development and meetings targeted at supporting the case manager/local school district representative
Assisting the school’s scheduler/programmer with programming all students with disabilities in accordance with their IEPs
In collaboration with the principal, scheduling paraprofessionals in accordance with students’ IEPs and 504 Plans

In order to be successful and achieve the above responsibilities, the Case Manager, must possess the following qualifications, as described:

Type Of Education

Completion of a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in special education or a Master’s degree in educational administration
A valid Professional Educator License (PEL) in one of the following areas: Special Education (PK-Age 21) endorsement or School Support Personnel endorsement with a supervisory endorsement

Type Of Experience And Number Of Years

Two or more years of experience in special education

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Expertise in special education curriculum and service provision
Knowledge of general education curriculum
Demonstrated understanding of the individual needs of students with disabilities from a variety of language and cultural backgrounds
Strong knowledge of federal and state laws and regulations regarding the delivery of special education and related services
Knowledge and understanding of CPS resources
Knowledge of intervention and assessment strategies for disabled and non-disabled students
Knowledge of multi-tiered systems of support (MTSS or RTI)
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with administrators, staff, students, parents, governmental and community agencies, and employers
Ability to problem-solve, work on a team, use data to guide work, and clearly communicate to multiple stakeholders
Demonstrated expertise in customer service, consensus building, and use of problem solving skills and strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills

jobs.description:
Description

Whole Foods Market is seeking a sharp, driven, and analytically minded Sr Program Manager to join our Promotions Analytics team. In this role, you will be at the forefront of understanding promotional performance and customer engagement, translating campaign data into strategic insights that directly shape our merchandising initiatives.

This is a high-visibility role with real impact from day one. The right candidate should have a strong foundation in retail merchandising and promotional strategy, possess the ability to dive deep into complex campaign performance metrics, understand the business context behind the data, and continuously strive to find deeper insights. They should be ready to step into a role guiding and developing a small analytics team. The 3 other members of the Promotions Analytics team will look to the Sr Program Manager to interpret leadership's intent, inform priorities, and provide coaching & development.

You will design and execute promotional analytics strategies to capture high-quality insights on retail promotions effectiveness and resulting customer behavior. You will conduct or manage deep-dive analyses on promotional performance, customer segmentation, and engagement patterns, surfacing the "so what" behind the data. Working closely with Merchandising and Marketing leaders, you will develop strategy, launch pilots, and deliver clear, actionable findings. Over time, you will help the team build repeatable, scalable analytical frameworks that improve the team's speed and depth. You will communicate results clearly to senior business leaders, translating complex data into concise narratives, and contribute as a key voice for the 3 other members of the Promotions Analytics team.

We are looking for a candidate who brings a strong foundation in retail merchandising and promotional strategy, with the ability to contextualize business performance data within broader market dynamics. They have a proven ability to work through complex performance metrics and extract meaningful, business-relevant insights. They are comfortable operating at both the detail level and the strategic level, knowing when each is needed. They consistently deliver timely, accurate analyses, build partnerships across business teams, and drive change through insight. They can distill complex findings into concise narratives for a range of audiences.

Promotions analytics is a strategic priority at Whole Foods Market. You'll have the opportunity to shape how we understand and optimize our promotional strategies, with the resources, data, and leadership support to make a real difference.

Key job responsibilities

Program Management: Manage priorities and project deliverable timelines for the Promotions Analytics team. Identify opportunities for the team to pursue supporting organizational goals. Own end-to-end delivery of promotional analytics initiatives from strategy through execution.

Collaboration & Relationships: Maintain close working relationships with Merchandising, Marketing, and cross-functional stakeholder leaders to collaborate on the development of promotional strategy and reporting needs. Work cross-functionally with product teams to design reporting capabilities using in-house tools. Partner with data engineering and business intelligence teams to ensure data quality and accessibility.

Communication: Speak, present, and train team members on promotional strategy, campaign optimization, and customer engagement insights. Manage regular updates to leadership on projects related to promotional performance and strategies. Present findings effectively to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

Analytics and Reporting: Gather and analyze promotional campaign data, customer behavioral data, and transactional data to provide strategic insights. Utilize analytical methods to identify patterns and trends across data sources. Ability to self-serve data with programming skills (SQL, R, Python). Experience in a highly scalable, distributed environment preferred. Analyze data to provide promotional strategy recommendations, highlight opportunities, and inform adjustments to merchandising initiatives. Provide coaching and development to team members on analytical approaches, stakeholder management, and business acumen.

Strategic Leadership: Serve as a go-to resource for Merchandising and Marketing teams on promotional performance questions. Contribute to quarterly program reviews to inform planning and optimization efforts. Drive process improvements and build scalable frameworks for promotional analytics. Provide guidance on work prioritization and analytical quality standards for the Promotions Analytics team.

Stay current with food, retail, market news, and natural products trends. Read popular and trade press widely.

A day in the life

You start your day reviewing promotional campaign performance data in SQL, identifying trends in customer engagement and product performance across multiple campaigns. You build strategic frameworks to evaluate promotional effectiveness and meet with Merchandising leaders to discuss insights for upcoming seasonal promotions. You lead a cross-functional meeting to present quarterly promotional performance results, guiding the team through customer segment analysis and ROI calculations. After managing priorities for your analytics team and addressing an ad-hoc request from Marketing leadership investigating regional promotional performance differences, you prepare a presentation for senior leadership on promotional strategy recommendations. You close the day by facilitating a team retrospective on the quarterly review process, coaching a team member on their stakeholder presentation approach, and documenting follow-up requests.

Basic Qualifications

2+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
5+ years of business intelligence and analytics experience
Experience with data scripting languages (e.g. SQL, Python, R etc.) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, or Matlab)
Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders
Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, analytical business specialty or commensurate retail experience

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in management, business administration, economics, engineering, marketing

new_jobs.description:
The Short Version

You will carry six to eight families. Not sixty. Not two hundred.

Part-time and hourly, or full-time and salaried: W-2 either way, and yours to grow at your own pace.

We have removed insurance mandates and hospital bureaucracy from the work. What that buys you is the rarest thing in modern medicine: the time to do the job the way you already know it should be done.

If that is the job you have been looking for, here is the rest of it.

The Role

Avoa Health is a private health advisory firm serving families on Chicago’s North Shore through serious diagnoses, complex conditions, and the challenges of aging. The Private Health Advisor is the single, trusted point of contact for those families. Their advocate. Their Healthcare Chief of Staff. The person who sees the problem coming before they do.

This is not case management. Case management is a caseload. This is a small number of families, held closely, over time.

Our clients are accustomed to excellence in every other part of their lives, and they expect the same standard here. One size fits one: every family receives a response built for them alone.

What You Will Do

Run central command.
You are the connective tissue between the family and their specialists, making sure every provider is aligned and the client’s agency is protected. You manage the scheduling, the records, the follow-up. Hushpitality is our word for doing that invisibly: the family experiences the result of your work without ever carrying the noise of it.
Vet the specialists. You evaluate physicians and institutions and find the right fit, not the nearest one.

Show up in the room.
You accompany clients to the appointments that matter, with the agenda prepared in advance, and you deliver a post-visit summary that turns jargon into a clear path forward.

Dismantle the roadblocks.
Pre-authorizations, denials, billing disputes. You absorb that friction so the family never feels it.

Build the scaffolding.
For clients facing cognitive decline or a difficult transition, you put discreet systems in place that preserve dignity while keeping them safe.

Own the problem.
Every issue is yours. When the system fails, you listen, you own it, and you fix it. You never say it is not your department.

Who This is For

You have five or more years in healthcare, ideally in advocacy, case management, oncology navigation, palliative care, or geriatric care. LPN, RN, or MSW is preferred and not mandatory.
You are warm. You are conscientious to the point that other people find it remarkable. You assume things will work out and you make them work out.

You can move from a technical conversation with a neurosurgeon to a briefing with a family office director without changing gear.

Your language is precise and generous. You know the difference between “I’ll try” and “I will see to it,” and so does the family listening.

You are comfortable with modern tools: secure video, shared calendars, the ordinary technology of a well-run firm. We provide the technology and the administrative backing so your attention stays on the families.

The Deal

Part-time roles are hourly. Full-time roles are salaried.
Both are W-2, which makes you a formal member of the team, not a contractor.
It grows at your pace.
Start part-time and grow into full-time as you and your client book are ready, or stay part-time for as long as it fits your life. Both are real, long-term seats.
Real control over your schedule, in both directions
. If you cannot take Tuesday mornings, we will not book you Tuesday mornings. In return, we ask for dependable daytime availability, since most of the work, care coordination and physician visits, happens in business hours, plus a willingness to help with the occasional off-hours emergency, which the team shares and covers together. We ask every advisor to hold at least one full day a week for Avoa Health, because that predictability is what lets us balance the work and protect everyone’s schedule. What you will not have is a pager, a quota, or a productivity metric.
Hybrid, roughly seventy percent remote
and thirty percent in person, flexing with what clients need. Our clients are concentrated on the North Shore, so plan on in-person meetings and physician visits in that area.
Travel is covered
. You will drive to client appointments; mileage between them is reimbursed at the standard IRS rate, and a company card covers authorized work expenses.
You are supported, not on your own
. Malpractice and liability coverage, secure technology, and full administrative backing, so your attention stays on the families rather than the overhead.
Full transparency before you invest an hour.
Before any formal interview, we put every parameter of the role in writing for you: compensation, schedule, technology, and the health and screening requirements. You will know exactly what you are considering before you commit your time. We think that is the only respectful way to do this.

Why Avoa Health

A return to the art of care
. You went into this work to help people, and somewhere along the way volume took the helping out of it. There is no volume here.

Autonomy with infrastructure
. You manage your own client portfolio. You operate with the independence of a private practitioner and none of the isolation, supported by the firm's systems and reputation.

Going above and beyond is the standard, and it is funded
. When you see what a family needs, you will not have to ask permission or find the budget.

Depth
. A handful of families, known well, over years. That is the entire proposition.

Helping develop and maintain recruitment materials and outreach initiatives.

A faithful, practicing Catholic

new_jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Whole Foods Market Promotions Analytics
new_jobs.description:
Description

Whole Foods Market is seeking a sharp, driven, and analytically minded Sr Program Manager to join our Promotions Analytics team. In this role, you will be at the forefront of understanding promotional performance and customer engagement, translating campaign data into strategic insights that directly shape our merchandising initiatives.

This is a high-visibility role with real impact from day one. The right candidate should have a strong foundation in retail merchandising and promotional strategy, possess the ability to dive deep into complex campaign performance metrics, understand the business context behind the data, and continuously strive to find deeper insights. They should be ready to step into a role guiding and developing a small analytics team. The 3 other members of the Promotions Analytics team will look to the Sr Program Manager to interpret leadership's intent, inform priorities, and provide coaching & development.

You will design and execute promotional analytics strategies to capture high-quality insights on retail promotions effectiveness and resulting customer behavior. You will conduct or manage deep-dive analyses on promotional performance, customer segmentation, and engagement patterns, surfacing the "so what" behind the data. Working closely with Merchandising and Marketing leaders, you will develop strategy, launch pilots, and deliver clear, actionable findings. Over time, you will help the team build repeatable, scalable analytical frameworks that improve the team's speed and depth. You will communicate results clearly to senior business leaders, translating complex data into concise narratives, and contribute as a key voice for the 3 other members of the Promotions Analytics team.

We are looking for a candidate who brings a strong foundation in retail merchandising and promotional strategy, with the ability to contextualize business performance data within broader market dynamics. They have a proven ability to work through complex performance metrics and extract meaningful, business-relevant insights. They are comfortable operating at both the detail level and the strategic level, knowing when each is needed. They consistently deliver timely, accurate analyses, build partnerships across business teams, and drive change through insight. They can distill complex findings into concise narratives for a range of audiences.

Promotions analytics is a strategic priority at Whole Foods Market. You'll have the opportunity to shape how we understand and optimize our promotional strategies, with the resources, data, and leadership support to make a real difference.

Key job responsibilities

Program Management: Manage priorities and project deliverable timelines for the Promotions Analytics team. Identify opportunities for the team to pursue supporting organizational goals. Own end-to-end delivery of promotional analytics initiatives from strategy through execution.

Collaboration & Relationships: Maintain close working relationships with Merchandising, Marketing, and cross-functional stakeholder leaders to collaborate on the development of promotional strategy and reporting needs. Work cross-functionally with product teams to design reporting capabilities using in-house tools. Partner with data engineering and business intelligence teams to ensure data quality and accessibility.

Communication: Speak, present, and train team members on promotional strategy, campaign optimization, and customer engagement insights. Manage regular updates to leadership on projects related to promotional performance and strategies. Present findings effectively to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

Analytics and Reporting: Gather and analyze promotional campaign data, customer behavioral data, and transactional data to provide strategic insights. Utilize analytical methods to identify patterns and trends across data sources. Ability to self-serve data with programming skills (SQL, R, Python). Experience in a highly scalable, distributed environment preferred. Analyze data to provide promotional strategy recommendations, highlight opportunities, and inform adjustments to merchandising initiatives. Provide coaching and development to team members on analytical approaches, stakeholder management, and business acumen.

Strategic Leadership: Serve as a go-to resource for Merchandising and Marketing teams on promotional performance questions. Contribute to quarterly program reviews to inform planning and optimization efforts. Drive process improvements and build scalable frameworks for promotional analytics. Provide guidance on work prioritization and analytical quality standards for the Promotions Analytics team.

Stay current with food, retail, market news, and natural products trends. Read popular and trade press widely.

A day in the life

You start your day reviewing promotional campaign performance data in SQL, identifying trends in customer engagement and product performance across multiple campaigns. You build strategic frameworks to evaluate promotional effectiveness and meet with Merchandising leaders to discuss insights for upcoming seasonal promotions. You lead a cross-functional meeting to present quarterly promotional performance results, guiding the team through customer segment analysis and ROI calculations. After managing priorities for your analytics team and addressing an ad-hoc request from Marketing leadership investigating regional promotional performance differences, you prepare a presentation for senior leadership on promotional strategy recommendations. You close the day by facilitating a team retrospective on the quarterly review process, coaching a team member on their stakeholder presentation approach, and documenting follow-up requests.

Basic Qualifications

2+ years of program or project management experience
Experience using data and metrics to determine and drive improvements
Experience owning program strategy, end to end delivery, and communicating results to senior leadership
5+ years of business intelligence and analytics experience
Experience with data scripting languages (e.g. SQL, Python, R etc.) or statistical/mathematical software (e.g. R, SAS, or Matlab)
Experience in written and verbal communication with the ability to present complex technical information in a clear and concise manner to executives and non-technical leaders
Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, analytical business specialty or commensurate retail experience

Preferred Qualifications

2+ years of driving process improvements experience
Master's degree, or MBA in management, business administration, economics, engineering, marketing
